origin.description: Coefficients (columns) are dropped from a design matrix to ensure that it has full rank.

arguments.name: X
arguments.text: a design matrix, e.g., the result of model.matrix possibly of less than full column rank, i.e., with redundant parameters. Works for ncol(X) >= 0 and nrow(X) >= 0.

arguments.name: silent
arguments.text: should a message not be issued if X is column rank deficient?

origin.details: Redundant columns of the design matrix are identified with the LINPACK implementation of the qr decomposition and removed. The returned design matrix will have qr(X)$rank columns.
origin.value: The design matrix X without redundant columns.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ordinal))
X <- model.matrix( ~ PRODID * DAY, data = soup)
ncol(X)
newX <- drop.coef(X)
ncol(newX)

translation.description: Coefficients (columns) are dropped from a design matrix to ensure that it has full rank.

arguments.name: X
arguments.text: a two-dimensional design matrix, possibly column rank deficient.

arguments.name: silent
arguments.text: suppress the rank-deficiency message when columns are dropped.

translation.details: Redundant columns are identified with R's LINPACK dqrdc2 (qr with LAPACK FALSE and tol 1e-7) and removed in pivot order.
translation.value: A copy of X with redundant columns removed.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from ordinal.drop_coef import drop_coef

X = np.load("proof/drop_coef_soup_X.npz")["X"]
print(X.shape[1])
newX = drop_coef(X)
print(newX.shape[1])
